master.one_liner: Use any node as a stamp: scan the window cheaply, then evaluate Source only K times per lane, with a rank-subtract fade so swapping candidates cannot pop.
master.look:
Scattered independent copies of any graph: rocks, lichen patches, moss clumps, islands of detail on a flat background, with random rotation and a per-copy seed. Clumped by a density source. Look test with 2-octave Perlin as the stamp reads as separate patches of texture, nothing like FBm.
[StampField, lit-classic] Prototype cl_stamp: hemispheres as a pile of pebbles or balls (dead leaves); Perlin discs as cloud puffs or lichen; stripes as rotated Gabor patches in Sum (classic spot noise) and fish-scale patchwork in Over; ring profiles as bubbles or craters. Layers 3+ close all gaps. Scales, rock litter, foliage clusters, craters, polka dots with jitter 0, and cyclostationary weaves.
master.algorithm:
Lattice = unit cells, window 3^dim. For each window cell: hash h, centre c = cell + 0.5 + Jitter*(rnd-0.5), radius r = Size*lerp(SizeMin,1,rnd) (clamp so reach <= 1 cell), d = p - c, mask m = (1 - sat(|d|^2/r^2))^3, multiplied by alive = rnd < Density. Per-lane partial selection (the same insertion-with-Select used by Cellular for F1..F4) keeps the K+1 largest masks with their d, r and h in K+1 register slots. Then wK = max(0, m_k - m_(K+1)): each kept stamp fades to exactly zero at the moment it would lose its slot, so the result stays C0 whatever K is. For k in 0..K-1 (constant loop): rotate d by the hash angle (2D: rational or table cos/sin; 3D: unit quaternion from hash bits), l = R*d/r, v_k = Source.Gen(seed = h_k, l...). Note that the seed and position differ per lane, which Gen already supports. Combine: Sum = sum(w_k v_k); Variance-preserving = sum(w v)/sqrt(sum w^2); PNorm max = (sum (w v)^4)^(1/4) via two sqrts. Polynomial MinSmooth/MaxSmooth is not associative, so it is order dependent and seams when the slot order changes; p-norm and sum are order independent and contribute exactly 0 at w=0. Density has two modes: AtCentre (Density source evaluated at c for each window cell, gives whole stamps, costs 3^dim evals) or AtSample (one eval at p, r *= density(p), stamps erode smoothly, 1 eval). Optional Source B/C/D with a hash-picked bank: every bank member is evaluated at each K slot and Selected.

[StampField, lit-classic] For layer l (scale Ratio^l), cell c in 3^d window: h=hash; site=c+.5+.7*(rnd-.5); radius Rr=lerp(Rmin,Rmax,rnd); r2=|x_l-site|^2/Rr^2; if r2<1 candidate.
u=Rot(rnd*Rotation)*(x_l-site)/Rr.
Sum: v+=G_i*(1-r2)^2*Source(seed^h,u).
Max: v=max(v,(1-r2)^2*(Source+offset)).
Over: keep per-lane best priority among covering stamps (prio=Layers-l+rnd); after the whole window call Source(seed^h_best,u_best) ONCE for each lane. Soft variant: top-2 and blend by r2.
Density source and Size source may be sampled at stamp centre (one extra eval per candidate) for stable shapes; sampling at x is cheaper.
master.why_new: CellularLookup samples at the site only, so stamps are flat. There is no way to place, rotate or occlude copies of a generator in a graph. Occlusion gives hard-edged, non-Gaussian structure the survey lists as an open direction. Worley's paper names bombing as the pre-basis-function approach; this makes it a pointwise node with any kernel.
master.simd_plan: Scan cost is about CellularDistance (9/27/81 cells) plus K+1 register slots of Select; rotation and Source evals happen only for the K winners. Estimate: 2D scan ~5 ns + K*Source; 3D ~15 ns + K*Source; 4D ~50 ns + K*Source. K is a constant int member. Dimension agnostic via GenT pack; 4D keeps GenTileable2D working, though 4D rotation should be reduced to two plane rotations. Stamps larger than a cell: use Feature Scale and accept lower density, because reach is capped at the window.
master.continuity: C0 verified in scalar proto: c0ratio 1.00 without the fade and 8.15 with rank-subtract at K=2, same seed. C1 is not guaranteed because of the kink at slot swaps.
master.params: Source (GeneratorSource), K (int 1..4), Size (hybrid, AtSample only), SizeMin, Density (hybrid, enum AtCentre/AtSample), Jitter, Rotation amount (hybrid), Mask profile enum, Combine enum, Sample Scale R (stamp zoom), Background constant
master.risks:
Low K with many overlaps thins the field, since all weights are reduced by m_(K+1) where stamps are dense. Density AtCentre in 3D is 27 evals of the density source. Range depends on combine mode, so normalise analytically for Sum and accept clamp for others. A source with strong DC offset produces visible discs; a Remove Mean option or an offset would help.
[Scatter, stamp-scatter] Cost multiplies with source cost and dimension (4D Wide = 81 source evals: must warn in the metadata). Hybrids evaluated at the stamp centre is a new convention for hybrids (CellularLookup sets precedent). Hash bits: two hashes per cell needed. Artists will ask for stamps bigger than rAllow; the clamp silently shrinks them, so expose rAllow in the description and suggest Octaves. Sum mode range depends on overlap count; normalise by measured constant per Window.
[StampScatter, repo-demand] Cost explodes for heavy sources (FBm source with 5 octaves: 9x5 octaves). AlphaOver in fixed order needs care to be seed-stable. Not prototyped directly; CellularDomain's look-test covers the transform part.
master.cost_note: Estimate: 2D scan ~5 ns + K*Source; 3D ~15 ns + K*Source; 4D ~50 ns + K*Source.
master.variant_notes: Any node as a stamp. Three cost strategies to compare: scan then K top-mask source evals with rank-subtract fade (cheapest C0), Over mode with one eval per lane, and full window x Source for true Sum. Source seed must respond per lane.

master.one_liner: Painterly strokes following a direction field from a single per-lane Source eval, composited in priority order: fur, feathers, impasto, grass.
master.look: Prototype: calligraphic tapered petals, flames and feathers that sweep together. Lane mode curves strokes like Van Gogh swirls; centre mode looks like straight scattered brush dabs. Bristle grooves show in hillshade. Very different from the contact sheet, closer to an illustration than to noise.
master.algorithm: Evaluate Direction source once per lane: th0 = Direction(p)*AngleRange. Window 3^dim of stroke features; for each cell: th = th0 + small hash offset. Frame: u = cos(th)*dx + sin(th)*dy, v = -sin(th)*dx + cos(th)*dy. Bend v -= b(h)*((u/L)^2 - 0.3). Taper t = sat(1-(u/L)^2). Absolute edge m = 1 - smoothstep(-E,0,|v| - W*sqrt(t) + (t>0?0:1)). Stroke surface: q = clamp(v/W, -1, 1); value = hash value*0.25 + 0.55*sqrt(1-q^2) + 0.15*sin(18*q + phase(h)) (bristle grooves). Priority per feature from hash; composite front to back as CollageStack (vis, col). Because th0 is the sample's angle, not the feature's, every stroke deforms into the field locally: the iso-orientation locus {p: p-c parallel to theta(p)} forms a curve through c. Alternative CentreAngle mode: Direction evaluated at each c, straight strokes, 9 evals.
master.why_new: Warped cellular or stretched noise has no discrete object edges, and no node has occlusion plus orientation. Single eval per lane gives a field-following look with only 1 Source eval, where LIC would need many integration steps and centre orientation needs one per cell.
master.simd_plan: 1 Direction eval + cos/sin once (shared across all cells: the rotation is per lane and can be reused, cheap), then 9 cells of frame arithmetic + selection ~10 ns in 2D. 3D is a real open question: direction needs a unit vector, three Direction sources or a Curl-like derived tangent; rods and elliptic flakes in 27 cells ~35 ns + 3 evals. 4D fallback: drop to 3D-direction plane, 81 cells.

Voxel scan per stone, seeds 991, 4242, 31337, 333-387 stones per config: 0.00% floating at default, tilt 0 and 1, steep hamp=3, very steep hamp=5 hfreq=1, rubble, flagstones. Flood fill of the voxelised vol cube, 112^3, 8 scenes: every disconnected piece touches the cube wall (a clipped stone), except one single voxel in bumpy rubble. X-ray slices show the embedded part. Not half buried at defaults though: exposed fraction .915 at sink .35, .504 at sink=1. Sink=0 is a tangent: 62.8% do not resolve into the ground, sink=.05 3.0%. master.one_liner: 3D stamps that sit on a heightfield source: rocks, hoodoos and stumps placed on terrain inside a density graph, pointwise, with no decoration pass.
master.look: Boulders, hoodoos, dolmen fields and tree-trunk stumps that are actually attached to the terrain's surface and follow it in 3D volumes, with undercut overhangs. Not prototyped: the look is inferred, and should be tested first.
master.algorithm: 3D sample (x,y,z), Up axis y. Column lattice in XZ only: window 3x3 (9 cells), not 27. For each column cell: hash h, centre (cx,cz) with jitter; ground height g = Height.Gen(seed, cx, cz), one eval per cell, at the feature rather than the sample. Stamp centre c = (cx, g + Sink*r, cz). Local d = p-c, optionally squashed in y. Tilt option: 2 extra Height evals per cell for a finite-difference normal, 27 evals in total, then rotate d into the slope frame so stones lie flush. Shape: analytic sphere or superellipsoid SDF, or capsule from (cx,g-Depth,cz) to (cx,g+Tall,cz) for pillars, or top-K Source in local coords for detailed rocks. Combine by Max SDF, or K=1 for the nearest. Union with the terrain density as usual: Output = max(terrainDensity, stampDensity) or Output only the stamps. Slope and altitude rules: alive = rnd<Density and g in [Min,Max], decided per feature with the same g, so nothing pops. 2D: side-view 1D column lattice with height from 1D line of Source. 4D: column lattice in x,z,w, 27 cells.
master.why_new: Voxel engines do this with a post-generation decoration pass that needs world state and chunk-border handling, which FastNoise's stateless model cannot do. Using column lattice and feature-centre height eval lets a density graph do it pointwise, with no seams at chunk borders. A hard thing made easy, and a very common request.
master.simd_plan: 9 column hashes + 9 Height evals (9x height source; with a 5-octave FBm Perlin ~50 ns, tilt triples this) + 9 SDF. Using column lattice is 3x cheaper than a 3D window; no Y search needed because each column holds exactly one stamp (a Stack Count constant gives more). Add GeneratorCache-like reuse is not possible across cells. Cost estimate 3D: ~5 ns + 9*Height + SDFs. 2D ~ 3 Height evals. Tiling with 4D is costly: 27*Height.
master.continuity: C0 for SDF or bump output that reaches zero at stamp reach and only depends on feature values. Height needs to be pure and non-sample-dependent, which it is at the column centre. A tall reach above 1 cell in y is fine because the column window is XZ only.

master.one_liner: A pointwise dead-leaves model: stacked layers of confined rounded stones where the first covering layer wins, giving real occlusion for gravel, rock piles and conglomerate.
master.look: Hillshade reads clearly as a pile of rounded stones, gravel or cobbles, with visible occlusion contours and T-shaped overlaps. Output mode with per-stone values gives clast mosaics like conglomerate.
master.algorithm: covered=false; out=0. For layer L (top first) in a fixed loop: P=Rot_L*x/(s0*g^L)+offset_L; C=floor(P); h=hash(C); R=0.3+0.2*r4; v=P-(C+R+(1-2R)*(r1,r2)); rotate v by an angle from the hash; asp=0.65+0.35*r5; q=(u/R)^4+(w/(R*asp))^4; inside=on & q<1; val=sqrt(max(1-q,0))*R*asp*s_L+0.15*r6*s_L+(Layers-L)*bias; out=Select(covered,out,Select(inside,val,out)); covered|=inside. The prototype used exponent 2.6; integer powers should be used in the port. Optional last layer: full F1 cell value, to guarantee coverage.
master.why_new: No existing node has occlusion: all cellular nodes partition space, and blends average or take min/max across a whole layer. Layer order gives stones sitting on stones, a look which needs painter's ordering in a graph.

master.one_liner: Overlapping oriented stamps where stacking order is the projection of each stamp centre onto the local flow, and only the winning stamp evaluates a source in its own frame: scales, feathers, roof tiles, trowel strokes.
master.look:
Look-tested (m=8). Fish or dragon scales with fine barbs that flow around a field and always overlap the right way, plus palette-knife stucco strokes with shape=1 and bend. Hard occluding edges give a hillshade no blend can produce. Chevron plus stretched Interior gives feathers; Stroke with low detail gives plaster; Disc with Min composite gives hammered dents.

master.algorithm: Lane dir d=(cos th,sin th) from hybrid Angle. For each candidate cell: centre c (stagger plus jitter), r=p-c, v=dot(r,d), u=dot(r,perp d), both divided by per-stamp size. Optional curvature v+=Bend*rnd*u^2 and chevron v+=Chevron*|u|. Inside test by Shape: Scale (u^2/a^2 + (v/(v>0?b:.55b))^2 <1), Stroke (max(|v|/b,|u|/w)<1), Disc. Priority = -dot(c,d) + PJ*rnd. Keep the highest-priority covering stamp: mask = inside AND prio>best, then Select best, u, v, hash. After the loop, one evaluation of optional Interior source at (u*Su+off_u(h), v*Sv+off_v(h)). Output = tilt profile (0.5-0.5*v/b for Scale; flat with raised rim for Stroke) + Detail*Interior + tone(h). Lanes with no stamp return Base.
master.why_new: Texture bombing has a fixed order or per-cell priority, so a flow-following shingle needs per-region ordering. Here the order comes from a float comparison computed per lane, so overlap direction follows the field automatically and any orientation works. The single post-selection eval keeps source cost at 1 regardless of window, which makes rich stamp interiors affordable, where CellularLookup only gives a constant per cell.
master.simd_plan: Masked loop, no per-candidate source. 2D: 4x4 window centred on the nearest lattice vertex (16 candidates, reach at least 1.5, stamps up to about 1.2 fit); 9 candidates only if stamp reach is below 1-jitter/2. About 1.5x CellularDistance plus 1 Interior: scalar 7x Perlin including the interior simplex. 3D: 27 candidates, ellipsoid stamps with reach below 0.8 and axis from Angle plus Tilt, about 1.5x CellularDistance 3D. 4D: 81 candidates, 4x CellularDistance 3D, Scale shape only.
master.continuity: Discontinuous by design at stamp edges (occlusion steps). Inside a stamp, continuous except where a fast-changing Angle reorders priorities. The look depends on hard edges, and a Softness option can fade the step over the last 10% of the stamp if C0 is needed.
master.params: Angle, Tilt, Size, Size Jitter, Bend, Chevron, Priority Jitter, Shape enum, Interior (generator), Interior Scale U/V, Detail, Base. Hybrid: Angle, Tilt, Size, Detail.
master.risks:
The proto used a 3x3 window with reach above 1, so small seams are possible; the port needs the 4x4 window. Coverage holes appear if Size is too small (visible black gaps in stroke mode). Rapidly curling fields can produce popping priority flips. Feature size is capped by the window.
[ShingleStack, cell-relations] Rare uncovered gaps appear as specks at r below coverage limit (seen in proto). The directional look in 3D needs a 3D direction, and in 4D tiling the direction has no clean meaning. Hillshade of discontinuous output is harsh as raw terrain.

master.one_liner: Stamps with sizes spanning orders of magnitude and no window at all: hash-driven quadtree descent to a leaf, then 1 stamp inside the leaf, linear in depth and same cost in 4D.
master.look: Prototype: large spots surrounded by clusters of small ones with a visible quadtree order; reads like tech greeble, circuit boards, mitotic cells, city blocks and starfields. Axis-aligned parent grouping is visible and is a signature; not an organic look unless warped or rotated.
master.algorithm: scale = 1, alive = all lanes. For d in 0..Depth-1 (constant count): i = floor(p*scale); h = hash(i, level d); leaf coords (for alive lanes) = p*scale - i - 0.5, saved via Select with leaf hash and leaf scale. alive &= rnd(h) < SplitProbability(d); scale = Select(alive, scale*2, scale). The result is one leaf per lane with lx in [-0.5,0.5]^dim. Stamp lies strictly inside the leaf: mask m = (1-t^2)^3 with t = |l-j|/(0.4*R), j = jitter bounded so that j+0.4R < 0.5. Output = m * Source.Gen(seed=h, Rot(h)*l*Zoom)/sqrt(scale)^Roughness, or analytic dome; also output leaf size as a mask. Hybrid SplitProbability sampled at the leaf's centre gives density-driven refinement: fine stamps where the source says.
master.why_new: Sizes spanning 1:32 in a window-based scatter would need a separate lattice per size and a window for each. Here it costs Depth hashes plus 1 Source eval, regardless of dimension. Fractal octaves stack everywhere and cannot drop large features where small ones go; this partitions space by level.
master.simd_plan: Loop of Depth iterations with floor, hash and masks: Depth=5 is ~5 hashes (~3 ns) + 1 stamp, in every dimension. 2D, 3D and 4D all ~4-6 ns + Source, the cheapest node here and the only scatter with no exponential window cost. Tiling via 4D is free of penalty. Rotation per stamp local.
master.continuity: C0: c0ratio 7.90 at depth 1 and 6.13 at depth 3, falling to 3.23 at depth 5 because tiny stamps have very steep slopes, not jumps. Requires mask reaching zero inside the leaf, enforced by bounding jitter + radius.
master.params: Depth (int), Split Probability (hybrid), Split Falloff per depth, Stamp Radius, Jitter, Rotation, Roughness (amplitude vs size), Source (optional), Output enum (stamp, leaf size, leaf hash)
master.risks: Axis-aligned hierarchy is visible, and DomainRotate only hides the absolute axis, not the squareness of the arrangement. Layer two rotated instances with Max to help. master.one_liner: Opaque cut-out sheets with a global depth order plus built-in contact shadow: leaf litter, slate, feathers, torn paper.
master.look:
Prototype reads immediately as a pile of autumn leaves with real occlusion; hillshade looks like a modelled layer. Other shapes give slate, flagstones, feathers, dragon scales, camouflage, paper collage. Output is piecewise smooth with steep contours, which is unlike anything on the contact sheet.
[OcclusionStack (DeadLeaves), lattice-kernels] Pebble piles, leaf litter, bubbles, roof shingles, overlapping coins, bokeh. Prototyped: coherent layered discs, with hillshade immediately reading as stacked stones. T-junction topology is unavailable in anything on the sheet.
master.algorithm:
Window 3^dim. Each cell has a stamp with rotation, size and priority pr = rnd(h) (a pure function of the feature, so any window sees the same order, no seams). Rotate into local (u,v). Shape SDF by enum, e.g. Leaf: t = 1-(u/L)^2, sd = (|v|/W - t)*W, sd = max(sd, |u|-L); also Superellipse, Ngon, Shard. Mask m = 1 - smoothstep(-Edge, 0, sd). Shadow s = 1 - smoothstep(0, ShadowWidth, sd). Interior value val = per-stamp hash value + vein term exp(-|v|*k) + slope*u, optionally + Source at local coords. Sort candidates by pr with a fixed sorting network (9 inputs = 25 comparators with Selects in 2D), or keep top K by pr among m>0 for 3D. Composite front to back: col += vis*m*(val*shade + (shade-1)*ShadowDark); shade *= 1 - ShadowStrength*s*(1-m); vis *= 1-m. Final col += vis*Background. Shingle mode: pr is replaced by the lexicographic row, so rows overlap like roof tiles or fish scales with no sort at all.

[ScatterPainter, stamp-scatter] Same per-cell instancing as Scatter, but each cell yields a triple (key, value, alpha): key = rnd01(h1) (Age mode), or -s (Smaller-on-top), or value itself (Height mode, which degenerates to Max); alpha = coverage envelope of the stamp (0 outside, 1 inside, smooth over EdgeWidth) times presence.
Sort the N = 2^d triples per lane with a fixed compare-exchange network: 4 elements -> 5 CEs, 8 -> 19 CEs, 16 -> 60 CEs. One CE = mask = keyA > keyB; swap keys/values/alphas with Select (3 Selects + 1 compare per CE).
Composite back to front (lowest key first): out = Background; for i in sorted order: out = lerp(out, value_i, alpha_i).
Because the loop count and the network are constants, this is fully data parallel. Octaves: composite octave results with the same rule, treating the whole coarse octave as 'older' (key offset per octave), so small features always overwrite big ones, matching how a crater field evolves.
Optional Crater mode: the stamp value is a *replacement height* inside the bowl and an *additive* rim outside it: out = lerp(out, value_i, alpha_i) + rim_i*(1 - alpha_i). This gives rims that sit on older terrain while bowls cut through it.
master.why_new: Overlap order and occlusion cannot be built from Max or MaxSmooth over any graph, because a graph has no per-instance identity. Compared with plain dead-leaves noise, the node adds shape, inner structure and shadows from upper sheets on lower ones, which give the depth cue that makes it read as an object pile.
master.simd_plan:
Analytic only: 9 cells with rotation and SDF, plus sorting network. Estimate 2D 10-14 ns (3x CellularDistance). 3D with top-K=3 selection: 27 cells ~30-40 ns. 4D top-K=3: 81 cells ~110 ns, usable only for tiling. Source input: evaluate only at the K top slots. Rotation via table or rational form, no atan2.
[ScatterPainter, stamp-scatter] Scatter cost plus the network: 2D 5 CEs (~25 ops), 3D 19 CEs (~95 ops), 4D 60 CEs (~300 ops, roughly +8 ns on top of the 4D Scatter cost); Wide 3x3 window needs a 9-element network (25 CEs) which is still fine in 2D; 27 and 81 element networks are not worth it, so Wide is 2D only or falls back to SoftOver. Registers: N triples live simultaneously (16x3 float32v in 4D) so 4D may spill on SSE; acceptable. Lattice window and 2D/3D/4D as Scatter.
master.continuity: C0 with Edge > 0, verified: c0ratio 8.16 in 2D with the full sort. Near-discontinuous contours by design as Edge approaches 0. Top-K truncation introduces very small pops only where more than K soft edges coincide.
master.params: Shape enum, Size, Aspect (hybrid), Edge softness, Shadow Width, Shadow Strength, Vein Strength, Order enum (Random/Rows), Rotation Spread (hybrid, so scales can align), Density, optional Source, Background, K in 3D+
master.risks:
Reach is capped at 1 cell, so sheets need size <= 1 and coverage depends on density; some background shows through at low size. Sorting network code per dimension is awkward: use insertion-based partial selection in 3D/4D. In 3D the sheets become ellipsoids or lenses and the look is less obvious, so 3D's value is unproven (the proto's 3D slice is a sheared 2D fake).
[OcclusionStack (DeadLeaves), lattice-kernels] Coverage gaps at low density need a background. Discontinuities alias, so offer an optional output that returns edge distance to antialias. Windows limit radius, so size distribution is bounded: no truly scale-free leaves in one node, only through stacking two.
master.cost_note: Estimate 2D 10-14 ns (3x CellularDistance). 3D with top-K=3 selection: 27 cells ~30-40 ns.
master.variant_notes: Dead leaves with a global priority. Options: plain top-wins Select (OcclusionStack, cheapest), sorting-network painter's over (ScatterPainter), and contact shadows from upper sheets (CollageStack, which is what makes it read as a pile).

master.one_liner: A volumetric Scatter specialised to signed distance stamps: randomly rotated superellipsoid boulders (and their 2D/4D analogues) combined with a polynomial smooth-min into an approximate SDF, so a threshold gives rubble, scree, debris in caves, asteroid interiors and rock walls with individual stones.
master.look: Individual stones with flat-ish faces (high e) or rounded pebbles (e=2), embedded or piled, each rotated differently; in 3D slices, discrete blobs of varying ellipticity; thresholded 3D: caves with rubble floors, boulder fields on asteroids, conglomerate rock cross sections, cobbled beds. SDF output also drives distance-based effects (moss in the crevices via Remap of d). The contact sheet has only smooth noises and cells; there are no bodies with silhouettes in 3D.
master.algorithm:
Scatter lattice in 3D (2^3 = 8 cells, rAllow rule). Per stamp: centre, Shoemake quaternion rotation from 3 hash uniforms, axis radii (a,b,c) = s * (1 + Aspect*rnd11) each, superellipse exponent e per node (2..8), per-stamp low-harmonic bumps: rEff = r*(1 + Bump*(rnd11*cos2 + rnd11*cos3 + rnd11*sin2)) using cosines of the local azimuth from (x/r, y/r) via the Chebyshev recurrence, plus a polar term from z/r (Legendre P2) for 3D lumpiness.
SDF per stamp: d_i = (|x/a|^e + |y/b|^e + |z/c|^e)^(1/e) - 1 scaled back by s (approximate distance, exact for e=2 after the usual sphere correction), minus the bump term.
Combine: smooth min with polynomial k: h = clamp(0.5 + 0.5*(d2 - d1)/k, 0, 1); d = lerp(d2, d1, h) - k*h*(1-h), folded over the 8 stamps; Background = Scatter's empty value is +rAllow (far). Output modes: SDF (raw signed distance, clamped to [-1,1] via ScaleOutput of [-s, rAllow]), Inside (smoothstep(-Edge, Edge, -d) = a density mask), Height2D (in 2D, the SDF interpreted as a height: boulders from above with correct silhouettes).
2D: superellipses; 4D: superellipsoid with 4 radii and two-plane rotation (so tiling works); the smooth-min is dimension free.
Optional ground coupling when used as terrain: because the output is a distance, Max(terrain, -d*height) places boulders on a terrain built elsewhere; the Scatter density hybrid (evaluated at the stamp centre, e.g. a slope mask of the terrain) controls where stones appear.
master.why_new: The generic Scatter node could compose this from Stamp(Boulder) with Min, but the specialised version is worth it: it keeps SDF semantics correct (smooth-min with a distance, not a value), builds the 3D rotation and harmonic bumps once per stamp, and avoids a virtual call per cell. SDF output is also a new kind of signal for FastNoise (usable for ray marching / voxel placement), which no node currently provides.
master.simd_plan: 3D: 8 cells x (2 hashes, quaternion build ~25 ops, rotate ~20, superellipse with Pow ~40, bumps ~20, smooth-min ~12) ~ 140 ops per cell, ~15-18 ns on AVX2 (close to Cellular 3D). 2D ~5 ns, 4D 16 cells ~45 ns. e=2 fast path avoids Pow. All branch free; Octaves give graded rubble sizes with the D^-2 law.
master.continuity: C1 (smooth-min of C1 distances except on the superellipsoid ridges where it is C0 for e>2); the rAllow clamp keeps it seamless.

master.one_liner: Exact nearest point on a Fermat spiral found in O(1) with four candidates in the local Fibonacci basis, with a fixed-point golden angle: sunflowers, pinecones, succulents, spiral scales.
master.look:
Look-tested (m=13): dense spiral parastichies with characteristic moire arms. 2D distance output is immediately sunflower or cactus. Combined with TileSplit Interior or CellularLookup style instancing, you get fields of rosettes, succulents, or pinecone scales using the local frame with FlowShingle-like profiles.
[PhyllotaxisCellular, lattice-kernels] The sunflower tessellation: cells arranged along interlocking clockwise and counter-clockwise spirals, cell size constant over the disc (equal-area), with F1 giving dimples, F2-F1 giving the scale/bract network and Index giving a radial age gradient. 3D: nested shells of near-hexagonal cells (pollen grains, pangolin, pineapple skins, golf balls) in a volume.
master.algorithm:
c=spacing. n=(x^2+y^2)/c^2. n0=round(n). th=atan_poly(y,x)/2pi. Choose Fibonacci pair F0,F1 from k=floor(log_phi(2.2*sqrt(n))), table lookup via a permute. Golden angle in fixed point: alpha(m)=m*0x61C88647 as uint32, which is exact for all m and needs no float. a0,a1=signed fraction of F0*G, F1*G. dth=signed fraction of th32-n0*G. Solve [F0 F1; a0 a1](i,j)=(n-n0,dth). Candidates m=n0+(floor(i)+e0)*F0+(floor(j)+e1)*F1 for e in {0,1}^2, mask m>=0. Each: position c*sqrt(m)*(cos,sin of alpha(m)), distance. Keep min with its m and local vector. Outputs: distance, rnd(hash m), scaled index (m/maxN, gradient from centre), or a local frame for scale shapes (u along radial).

[FibonacciCellular, lit-recent] Params: PointCount N (int), Jitter (float 0..1), Output enum {F1, F2minusF1, CellValue, CellIndex}, Distance enum.
3D (direction cells): n = normalise(p) (radius ignored, or used as a seed slice via hash(floor(|p|)) for 'layered shells'). Spherical Fibonacci point i: z_i = 1 - (2i+1)/N, phi_i = 2pi * frac(i*PHI). Inverse mapping (Keinert): k = max(2, floor(log(N*pi*sqrt5*(1-n.z^2)) / log(PHI^2))); Fk = round(PHI^k/sqrt5), Fk1 = round(Fk*PHI); build the 2x2 basis B from (Fk, Fk1): B = [[2pi*frac((Fk+1)*PHI-1) - 2pi*(PHI-1), same for Fk1],[-2Fk/N, -2Fk1/N]]; c = round(B^-1 * (phi_n, n.z - (1-1/N))); the 4 candidates i = Fk*(c.x+s.x) + Fk1*(c.y+s.y) for s in {0,1}^2; reconstruct each candidate point, jitter it by Jitter * tangent rnd(hash(seed,i)) (keep within half the inter-point spacing ~ sqrt(4pi/N)/2), pick the nearest (F1) and second nearest (F2) by angular/chord distance.
2D (planar spiral cells): Vogel point i: r_i = sqrt(i/N)*Rmax... use r_i = c*sqrt(i), theta_i = 2pi*i*(PHI-1); inverse: with k from log of (pi*r^2), same Fibonacci-basis trick in (theta, r^2) space (the planar spiral is the sphere mapping with z replaced by r^2), 4 candidates, pick nearest. Points are capped: beyond the max index the domain tiles with an ordinary jittered grid (Select) so far coords stay cheap.
F1 normalised by the mean nearest spacing; CellValue = rnd11(hash(seed,i)).
master.why_new: Nothing on the sheet has rotational order or spirals. The usual approach searches a large index range; here the 2x2 solve gives 4 candidates, verified against a 4000 candidate brute force with only 0.004% of pixels differing. Spirals are normally thought of as unreachable from a hash lattice.
master.simd_plan: 1 atan poly, 1 log (or use float exponent extraction for k), 4 candidates each with sin, cos and sqrt. Int multiply gives exact angle. Measured 1.7x Perlin scalar (float32 m is enough). No hash at all except for output value. 3D: pinecone mode, z scales the spacing (conical stack) or spherical Fibonacci inverse for shells (from memory: Keinert et al. 2015, same local-basis trick on the sphere). 4D: w as extra spacing modulation, so a real function exists but torus tiling is not meaningful.
master.continuity: C0 for F1 distance if candidates contain the true nearest (measured c0ratio about 36, smooth). Value and local frame outputs are discontinuous at Voronoi walls as with any cell value. A very rare miss creates tiny discontinuities (0.004% differ, max image difference 70/255).
master.params: Spacing (hybrid would move all points, so better fixed), Output enum (Distance, Value, Index), Max Radius with fade, Angle Offset. Mainly per-node floats; Seed changes rotation only.
master.risks:
Non-stationary: a single centre at origin, needs DomainOffset or TileSplit Interior to instance. Not stationary coherent noise, so it may feel niche. Dimension story for 3D and 4D is the weakest of the list. Candidate misses increase near k switches. Small n near centre needs mask care. Index beyond 2^31 is out of scope, which is far beyond practical radius.
[FibonacciCellular, lit-recent] float32 precision of k and the Fibonacci basis for N > ~1e5 (paper discusses GPU precision fixes); 2D far-from-origin behaviour needs the fallback lattice; F2 is only approximately exact from 4 candidates.
